facts.statement: Atacamatitan is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaurs that lived in the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Atacamatitan (meaning "Atacama Desert titan") is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaurs from the Late Cretaceous Tolar Formation of Chile.

facts.statement: Chilean and Brazilian researchers began preliminary fossil hunting expeditions in the Antofagasta Region of Chile in February 2000.
facts.quote: In February 2000, with the purpose of looking for Mesozoic fossils in Chile, Chilean and Brazilian researchers mounted a preliminary expedition that was organized by the Chilean National Museum of Natural History and the National Museum of Brazil heading to Antofagasta Region.

facts.statement: Atacamatitan was named and described by Alexander et al. in 2011.
facts.quote: Atacamatitan was later named and described by Alexander et al. 2011, becoming one of the most complete titanosaurs known from Chile.

facts.statement: Thomas Holtz estimated the possible weight of Atacamatitan to be between 8 and 16 tonnes.
facts.quote: Although the body estimates are quite uncertain, Thomas Holtz estimated its possible weight between 8 and 16 t.

facts.statement: The gracile nature of the preserved femur suggests that Atacamatitan had stronger forelimbs than its hindlimbs.
facts.quote: The preserved right femur is more gracile compared to other elements, indicating that the animal had stronger forelimbs.

facts.statement: The preserved right femur of Atacamatitan measures 1.10 meters in length.
facts.quote: It measures 1.10 m, the femoral head is missing and posteriorly, it preserves a well developed fourth trochanter, extending to the proximal quarter.

facts.statement: Atacamatitan fossils were found in the Atacama Desert in northern Chile.
facts.quote: Fue encontrado en lo que ahora es el desierto de Atacama, en el norte de Chile

facts.statement: In its original description, Atacamatitan was classified within the family Titanosauridae.
facts.quote: In the original description, Atacamatitan was placed in the Titanosauridae.

facts.statement: A 2012 cladistic analysis by Rubilar-Rogers and Gutstein placed Atacamatitan within the clade Lithostrotia.
facts.quote: Nevertheless, in 2012, Rubilar-Rogers and Gutstein conducted a preliminary cladistic analysis which ended in a polytomy within Nemegtosaurus, Rapetosaurus, Titanosaurus and the Saltasauridae. Atacamatitan was placed within the Lithostrotia.

facts.statement: Atacamatitan belongs to the unranked superfamily Titanosauria.
The time range for Atacamatitan is estimated from the Cenomanian to the Maastrichtian, between 100.5 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Maastrichtian (100.5 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Most cladistic analyses exclude Atacamatitan due to the fragmentary nature of the holotype.
facts.quote: However given the fragmentary nature of the holotype, most cladistic analysis exclude Atacamatitan.

rejected.statement: The holotype specimen of Atacamatitan, cataloged as SGO-PV-961, was discovered during a second expedition in July 2001.
rejected.quote: The results ended on the discovery of the holotype of Atacamatitan: SGO-PV-961.

rejected.statement: Atacamatitan is characterized by dorsal vertebrae with curved pleurocoels that do not point posteriorly.
rejected.quote: According to Kellner et al. 2011, Atacamatitan can be recognised in having dorsal centra with pleurocoels that are curved and do not point posteriorly.
